decisions.diagnosis: Westbound sensor fault producing continuous false counts through the night, ending mid-afternoon on 14 Oct.
decisions.evidence: Daily raw 182, 244, 915 against a usual 15-30; night (00:00-05:30) counts of 81, 108 and 288 against 0-2 normally, 10-20 per 15-minute slot at 01:00-04:00 and one slot of 82; eastbound 320 normal on the same days (49, 13, 38).

decisions.diagnosis: Westbound ran at about twice its usual level with some night-time counts, possibly the same sensor fault that failed outright in October, but the counts look ride-like.
decisions.evidence: 321 daily 30-90 (one day 167 with bursts of 10-24 per slot in the evening of 21 Aug) against 15-20 before and after; night counts of 4-11 on many days against 0-1 normally; 320 unchanged at about 20.

decisions.diagnosis: Every record was published twice (8 records per slot instead of 4, in identical pairs); eastbound 320 was halved automatically but westbound 321 was missed.
decisions.evidence: Channels show pairs such as [0,0,1,1,0,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,0,0,0,6,6]; 321 has 0 odd slots on every day in the period; the same doubling starts in the middle of 12 Apr (slot 42-44) and carries on into counter 274 until 22 Jun.

decisions.diagnosis: Duplicated records begin partway through the day (from about 10:30), so the afternoon is double-counted but the morning is not; halving the whole day would be wrong.
decisions.evidence: 4 records per slot to slot 41, 8 (identical pairs) from slot 42 (320) and 44 (321); 320 raw 55 and 321 raw 33, about 1.5 times the usual level.

decisions.diagnosis: Duplicated records end partway through the day (to 11:45), so the morning is double-counted and the afternoon is not.
decisions.evidence: 8 records per slot (identical pairs) to slot 47, then 4; 676 raw 42 and 678 raw 38 against 13-30 on the following days.

decisions.diagnosis: Every record was published twice on this day; the automatic fix dropped the copies for 678 but not for 676.
decisions.evidence: 8 records per slot in identical pairs; 676 raw 44 with 0 odd slots against 9-20 on the days around it; 678 was fixed from 60 to 30.

decisions.diagnosis: Every hourly record was published twice; the duplicates were dropped for 678 but not for 676.
decisions.evidence: 8 records in the hourly slots in identical pairs (e.g. [38,38,0,0,9,9,0,0]); 676 raw 850 with 0 odd slots against about 400 normally; 678 was fixed from 612 to 306.

decisions.diagnosis: Every hourly record was published twice in both directions, and the automatic fix missed it.
decisions.evidence: 8 records in the hourly slots in identical pairs (e.g. [0,0,38,38,0,2,2,0]); 676 raw 708 and 678 raw 462, both with 0 odd slots, against about 390 and 260 normally.

decisions.diagnosis: After a three-month outage counter 274 came back reporting hourly and about 15 times higher than before, which could be a new or changed flow or a reinstalled sensor counting something different; the data cannot settle which.
decisions.evidence: 676/678 about 16-22/33 per day to May 2023, then 350/250 per day from 19 Aug 2023; records are now hourly-binned; the adjacent road counter at site 254 (20 m away) stayed at about 220/80 through the same outage with no step; weekend counts are higher than weekday counts; the best daily correlation with any nearby counter is only 0.81 (Alexandra Canal), so it is not another site's feed.

series.name: Eastbound (citybound)
series.evidence: 274 took over the day after 223 stopped (31 May / 1 Jun 2022), and the same duplicate-record fault runs straight across the handover; both East directions have an 8am peak, and the levels match (320 about 19-23 per day in early 2022, 678 about 15-23 per day in mid-2022).

series.name: Westbound
series.evidence: Straight handover on 1 Jun 2022; both West directions peak at 15:00-17:00; the levels match (321 about 16-21, 676 about 13-17 per day).

series.name: Eastbound (from Aug 2023)
series.evidence: Kept separate because the counter came back after a three-month outage reading about 10 times higher, in hourly bins, while the adjacent road counter showed no change; it is not clear that it reads comparably to the earlier data.

series.name: Westbound (from Aug 2023)
series.evidence: Kept separate because the level jumped about 20 times (17 to 350 per day) after the Apr-Aug 2023 outage, with a new hourly reporting format.

summary: A low-volume shared path (about 15-40 bikes per day) counted by 223 from 2012 to May 2022 and by 274 after it with no gap. The problems are duplicated records the automatic fixes missed (321 in Apr-May 2022, and single days in 2023-2024) and a three-day westbound sensor fault in Oct 2014. After an outage in Apr-Aug 2023, 274 came back reporting hourly at about 15 times the earlier level while the road counter next door did not change, so that period is flagged uncertain and kept as separate series.
